info.title: Privatus Analytics API
info.description: Every page in Privatus Analytics is also an API endpoint: add .json to the URL and send an API token as a Bearer token. Most of them are MCP tools too.

post.summary: Create an API token (the token is returned once)
post.description: Creates an API token for the calling member in a workspace and returns the secret exactly once in the token field. Copy it immediately, it cannot be read again and a lost token must be revoked and recreated. A token can only narrow what its member may do. permissions defaults to all of the member's own permissions when omitted (an explicit empty list is refused, and asking for a permission you lack is an error). site_ids takes public site ids (pa_...) and restricts the token to those sites, and when empty the token works for every site its member can access (or keeps the site list of the token making this call). expires_at is optional ISO 8601 and must be in the future and at most 3 years away, omit it for a token that never expires. allowed_ips limits the token to those IPs or CIDR ranges. A token making this call needs tokens.manage. A workspace that requires two-factor authentication refuses tokens for members without a second factor of their own. Returns the same fields as api_tokens_list plus token.

anyOf.description: The token itself: only returned when created

token_prefix.description: First characters, to recognize the token

owner.description: Email of the member who owns it

site_ids.description: Restricted to these sites (empty = all)

anyOf.description: MCP client that received it

name.description: A label to recognize the token by, for example CI deploys. Required.

permissions.description: Permission names to grant, from analytics.read, analytics.export, content.write, sites.manage, uptime.manage, members.manage, tokens.manage, billing.manage and workspace.manage. Must be a subset of your own. Omit to grant all of yours. An empty list is refused.

site_ids.description: Public site ids (pa_..., from sites_list) the token may access. Empty means every site its member can access.

expires_at.description: Expiry as an ISO 8601 timestamp, for example 2027-01-31T00:00:00Z. Must be in the future and at most 3 years away. Omit for a token that never expires.

allowed_ips.description: IP addresses or CIDR ranges (for example 203.0.113.7 or 198.51.100.0/24) the token accepts requests from. Empty means any address.

get.summary: List API tokens
get.description: Lists the API tokens of a workspace, newest first and paginated. Without the tokens.manage permission you only see your own tokens, with it you see every member's. Revoked and expired tokens are hidden unless include_revoked is true. Each item has id (uuid, used by api_tokens_delete), name, token_prefix (the first characters, for recognizing a token), owner (the member's email), permissions (names such as analytics.read), site_ids (public site ids pa_..., an empty array means every site the owner can access), allowed_ips, oauth_client (the connected app's name when the token was issued through OAuth, otherwise null), status (active, expired or revoked), expires_at, last_used_at, revoked_at and created_at. The secret itself is never returned here, token is always null in a list. It is only shown once by api_tokens_create.

schema.description: Set true to also list revoked and expired tokens. Default false.

anyOf.description: The token itself: only returned when created

token_prefix.description: First characters, to recognize the token

owner.description: Email of the member who owns it

delete.summary: Revoke an API token
delete.description: Revokes an API token immediately and permanently. Requests that use it fail from then on, and a revoked token cannot be restored, create a new one instead. The token record stays in the list with status revoked (use api_tokens_list with include_revoked to see it), and revoking an already revoked token changes nothing. Take the id (a uuid) from api_tokens_list. You can revoke your own tokens, revoking someone else's needs tokens.manage and reach over every site the token covers. A token calling this needs tokens.manage. Returns the revoked token without its secret.

get.summary: Get your profile and preferences
get.description: Returns the signed-in member's own profile and preferences. Use it to read settings before changing them with account_update. This is about the person, not a workspace. Workspace plan and invoices are under billing_get. Fields are email, unconfirmed_email (set while an email change awaits confirmation, otherwise null), name (nullable), theme (system, light or dark), default_landing (sites or last_site), locale (language code for the signed-in app), timezone (IANA name, nullable), shortcuts_enabled, reduce_motion, product_emails, site_audit_emails, marketing_emails, newsletter (all booleans where true means subscribed), two_factor (boolean), passkeys (count of registered passkeys) and created_at (ISO 8601). A session opened only through a workspace identity provider sees just email and the display settings.

email_verified.description: Whether the person has proven the email address is theirs. A client that logs people in with this account relies on it

anyOf.description: New email awaiting confirmation

locale.description: Language code of the app for this account (en by default)

menu_stars.description: The sidebar items this account starred, as keys such as site.experiments or workspace.billing

holiday_looks.description: The holiday looks this account sees in the app, as keys such as halloween or christmas

site_audit_emails.description: Whether site audit summary emails may be sent. Off here turns them off for every site

marketing_emails.description: Whether marketing emails (drip campaigns) may be sent. false after an unsubscribe

patch.summary: Update your profile and preferences
patch.description: Updates the signed-in member's own profile, display preferences and email subscriptions. Only the inputs you send change, everything else stays as it is. Changing email does not take effect at once. A confirmation email is sent to the new address (rate limited) and unconfirmed_email shows the pending address until it is confirmed. API tokens cannot change the email address and cannot turn marketing_emails back on after an unsubscribe, both need a signed-in browser. Turning marketing_emails off is allowed. Sessions opened by a workspace identity provider may only change the display settings (theme, default_landing, locale, timezone, shortcuts_enabled, reduce_motion). Returns the updated account in the same shape as account_get. This does not delete the account and cannot change workspace settings.

post.summary: Create an alert
post.description: Creates an alert rule that watches a site (or the whole workspace for kind usage) and notifies the chosen channels when it triggers. Path takes workspace_id. name and kind are required. kind decides what else is needed. threshold needs site_id, metric (visitors, visits, pageviews, bounce_rate or conversion), operator (gt, gte, lt or lte) and threshold, and conversion also needs goal_id. anomaly needs site_id and metric (visitors, visits or pageviews), compares the last window with the same window in each of the previous 4 weeks and uses sensitivity (low, medium or high). operator lt only alerts on drops, gt only on spikes and empty on both. goal needs site_id, goal_id and threshold (completions in the window). no_data needs site_id and threshold in hours without events (default 24). usage needs no site and threshold as percent of the monthly event allowance (default 80). uptime needs site_id and optionally uptime_check_id (default all checks of the site). ssl needs site_id and threshold in days before a certificate or domain expires (default 14). vitals needs site_id, metric (lcp, inp, cls, fcp or ttfb) and threshold in milliseconds (a score for cls). subscriptions needs site_id, metric (mrr_drop: MRR fell by more than threshold percent in the last 30 days, churn_rate or mrr_churn_rate: churn over the last 30 days is above threshold percent) and threshold (default 10), and skips while the site has no payment provider connected or nothing to measure. window_minutes (default 60, 5 to 10080) is how far back each evaluation looks. channel_ids come from notification_channels_list and sensitivity defaults to medium. Alerts are evaluated automatically every 5 minutes. bounce_rate and conversion thresholds are percents from 0 to 100. testimonials needs site_id and metric, which says what it watches: new (a new testimonial arrives), low_rating (a rating of 3 or lower arrives), approved (a testimonial is approved), allowance (the month's allowance of new testimonials is 80% used, used up, or holding a testimonial as waiting), sync_found (a sync finds new reviews), import_failed (an import fails, or a source fails three syncs in a row), removal_requested (someone asks for their testimonial to be removed) or request_bounced (a request email bounces). A testimonials alert is not evaluated every 5 minutes: it triggers at once each time the thing happens, records an incident that is already resolved, and its state stays ok. With metric allowance it watches the whole workspace and keeps no site. Returns the created alert with state ok.

metric.description: threshold: visitors, visits, pageviews, bounce_rate or conversion. anomaly: visitors, visits or pageviews. vitals: lcp, inp, cls, fcp or ttfb. subscriptions: mrr_drop, churn_rate or mrr_churn_rate. testimonials: what the alert watches, one of new (a new testimonial arrives), low_rating (a rating of 3 or lower arrives), approved (a testimonial is approved), allowance (the month's allowance of new testimonials is 80% used, used up, or holding a testimonial as waiting), sync_found (a sync finds new reviews), import_failed (an import fails, or a source fails three syncs in a row), removal_requested (someone asks for their testimonial to be removed) or request_bounced (a request email bounces). The default is new. Not used by the other kinds

operator.description: Comparison against the threshold: gt (greater), gte, lt (less) or lte. Required for threshold. For anomaly lt alerts only on drops, gt only on spikes and empty on both. vitals defaults to gt

threshold.description: Number whose unit depends on kind. threshold: the metric value (bounce_rate and conversion in percent 0 to 100). With a comparison it is a percent change. goal: completions in the window. new_referrer: visitors the new site sent in the window (default 10). no_data: hours without events (default 24). usage: percent of the allowance (default 80). ssl: days left (default 14). vitals: milliseconds (a score for cls). subscriptions: a percent (default 10). Not used by anomaly and uptime

window_minutes.description: How far back each evaluation looks, in minutes, from 5 to 10080 (default 60). For anomaly it is also the length of the windows compared with the previous 4 weeks

sensitivity.description: anomaly only: low, medium (default) or high. Higher is more sensitive and triggers on smaller deviations

goal_id.description: Goal id (goal_..., from goals_list) of the same site. Required for goal alerts and for threshold alerts with metric conversion

filters.description: threshold, anomaly, goal and new_referrer: count only the visits these filters match, as a list of [dimension, operator, value] in the same format as the stats tools, for example [["page","starts_with","/blog"]]. Empty or left out counts all visits. Ignored by the other kinds

segment_id.description: threshold, anomaly, goal and new_referrer: a shared segment (seg_..., from segments_list) of the same site whose filters are applied as well. A private segment is refused

comparison.description: threshold only: previous_period (the window just before) or previous_week (the same window a week earlier). The threshold is then a percent change and must be above 0: operator lt or lte triggers on a drop of at least that percent, gt or gte on a rise. Leave out to compare with a fixed value

min_rating.description: new_referrer only: the lowest Domain Rating (0 to 100) the referring domain needs to trigger the alert. Leave out for any referrer

frequency.description: testimonials alerts only: how often the alert notifies its channels. immediate (default) sends each time it happens, hourly sends one summary at the top of the next hour and daily one summary a day at 9:00 in the workspace's time zone. Every incident is in the history at once either way. Ignored for every other kind, which always notifies at once

enabled.description: Evaluate this alert (default true). Evaluation runs every 5 minutes. A testimonials alert is not evaluated: it triggers when the thing happens

kind.description: What to watch: threshold (a metric against a fixed value, or its change against an earlier window with comparison), anomaly (unusual compared with the last 4 weeks), goal (completions of a goal), new_referrer (a site that sent nothing in the 30 days before now sends visitors), no_data (no events for some hours), usage (share of the monthly event allowance), uptime (an uptime check is down), ssl (certificate or domain expires soon), vitals (a Web Vital is too slow), subscriptions (MRR falls or churn rises, from the Subscriptions page) or testimonials (something happens in the Testimonials of the site: metric says what)

post.summary: Ask a question in a new conversation (counts toward the monthly AI questions limit)
post.description: Starts a new Ask conversation on one site and answers its first question using that site's analytics. Use it for a plain-English question about a site. Use assistant_ask_followup to continue an existing conversation and the stats tools when you already know the exact query. The answer is produced by an AI model that runs read-only analytics queries on its own, so the call can take many seconds. It counts as one AI question against the workspace's monthly allowance (5 on Free, 20 on Pro, 100 on Business) and fails with a limit error when the allowance is used up. Paginated with page and per_page (maximum 100). It lists transactions only. To get the PDF call billing_invoices_get, and to update the card use billing_payment_method. Requires billing.manage.

get.summary: Get the PDF link for an invoice
get.description: Returns a link to the PDF invoice of one billed transaction. Get the invoice id from billing_invoices_list (the id field, a Paddle transaction id). The result has kind (invoice) and url, which is a link to the PDF from Paddle, so fetch or share it soon after the call. Fails if the id does not belong to this workspace or Paddle has no invoice for it. Requires billing.manage.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the item to act on, the id field returned by billing_invoices_list

anyOf.description: Short-lived Paddle URL

get.summary: Advanced Bot Detection report: hits on the site's honeypot pages, by page and by what gave the bot away
get.description: Reports the hits on the site's honeypot pages. A honeypot page is a page reached only through a hidden link and set up as the Advanced Bot Detection page in the app shows. These hits are bots, so they are never pageviews or visits and do not appear in stats_overview or stats_breakdown. Choose the range with period (7d, 30d (default), 90d or 12mo). Hits are kept for 12 months. The result has period, from (the start of the range), has_data (false until the first hit), totals (hits, distinct pages, automated (hits where the tracker saw an automated browser) and no_interaction (hits with no pointer, key or touch input)), pages (up to 50 rows with path, hits and last_hit_at), reasons (hits per result of the standard bot filter: known_bot, automation, datacenter, empty_user_agent, referrer_spam, or undetected for a hit the filter would have counted as a person) and recent (the latest 50 hits with occurred_at, path, country, browser, device, bot_reason, automation and interacted). No IP address or User-Agent is kept with a hit, only keyed hashes of them that can't identify anyone, and those are never returned. Needs analytics.read and the Business or Enterprise plan (402 plan_limit otherwise).

schema.description: Date range in the site's timezone: 7d, 30d (default), 90d or 12mo. Hits older than 12 months are deleted

post.summary: Set the spend for a campaign in a month
post.description: Records ad spend for one campaign in one month, so campaigns_list can show cost per acquisition and return on ad spend. If an entry for the same campaign and month already exists it is replaced, not duplicated, so this is also safe to call twice. campaign is the utm_campaign value as it appears in your tracked links, month is YYYY-MM (a full date such as 2026-09-15 is accepted and snaps to the first of the month), and amount is in major units as a number (1250.50, not minor units). currency is an optional 3-letter ISO code and defaults to the site currency. The response returns the stored entry with amount_minor in minor units. For many rows at once use campaign_costs_import. Needs content.write. Needs the Business or Enterprise plan (402 plan_limit otherwise).

campaign.description: The utm_campaign value the spend belongs to, exactly as used in your tracked links (e.g. spring_sale). Matching is case-insensitive when listing. One entry exists per campaign and month, saving again replaces the amount

month.description: Month the spend is for as YYYY-MM (e.g. 2026-09). A full date such as 2026-09-15 is accepted and snaps to the first of that month

amount.description: Spend for the month in major currency units as a number, e.g. 1250.50 for 1,250.50. Not minor units. Must not be negative

currency.description: 3-letter ISO 4217 code in capitals, e.g. USD. Defaults to the site currency

get.summary: List campaign cost entries
get.description: Lists the ad spend entries recorded for a site, newest month first, then by campaign name. Each row is one campaign in one month with amount_minor (an integer in minor currency units, so 125050 means 1,250.50), currency (ISO 4217, uppercase), month as YYYY-MM, and the entry id (a UUID, use it for campaign_costs_update and campaign_costs_delete). Pass campaign to see one campaign only (case-insensitive match on the utm_campaign value). Paginated with page and per_page (max 100). Costs feed CPA and ROAS in campaigns_list, so this is where to check what spend a campaign has. Needs analytics.read. Needs the Business or Enterprise plan (402 plan_limit otherwise).

schema.description: Only entries for this utm_campaign value (case-insensitive exact match)

delete.summary: Delete a campaign cost entry
delete.description: Permanently deletes one spend entry, found by its id from campaign_costs_list. This cannot be undone, and CPA and ROAS for that campaign and month stop including the spend right away. Other months and campaigns are not touched. Returns the deleted entry. Needs content.write. Needs the Business or Enterprise plan (402 plan_limit otherwise).

patch.summary: Change a campaign cost entry
patch.description: Changes an existing spend entry, found by its id from campaign_costs_list. Only the inputs you send change, so send just amount to correct a number. amount is in major units (1250.50) and is stored as minor units, month is YYYY-MM, currency is a 3-letter ISO code. Changing campaign or month to a combination that another entry already has fails with a validation error instead of merging. To correct spend for a campaign and month without knowing the id, call campaign_costs_create, which replaces the existing entry. Needs content.write. Needs the Business or Enterprise plan (402 plan_limit otherwise).

post.summary: Import campaign costs from CSV (campaign,month,amount[,currency])
post.description: Bulk-imports ad spend from CSV, the quick way to load many campaigns and months. Send the CSV text in csv (best for tools and API calls) or upload a file in file (multipart only). The first row must be a header containing campaign, month and amount, with an optional currency column, for example campaign,month,amount,currency then spring_sale,2026-09,1250.50,USD. Month is YYYY-MM, amount is in major units, currency defaults to the site currency. Rows upsert by campaign and month, so re-importing the same file does not duplicate. Limits are 1 MB and 5,000 rows. A bad row does not stop the import. The response has imported (count saved), failed (count rejected) and errors (the first 50 messages, each naming its row, where row 2 is the first data row). A missing header column, an oversized file or malformed CSV fails the whole request. Needs content.write. Needs the Business or Enterprise plan (402 plan_limit otherwise).

file.description: CSV file upload, multipart requests only. Max 1 MB and 5,000 rows. Send csv instead when calling through MCP or JSON

csv.description: CSV text with a header row containing campaign, month and amount, plus an optional currency column. Example: campaign,month,amount,currency then spring_sale,2026-09,1250.50,USD. get.summary: Build and validate a UTM-tagged URL
get.description: Builds a UTM-tagged URL for a landing page and checks the values. Nothing is saved and no data is read, so it is safe to call repeatedly. Pass destination (a full https:// URL) plus utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content and utm_term as needed, or pick a preset (newsletter, social, paid_search and so on) to fill utm_source and utm_medium when you leave them blank. Returns url (null when there is an error), valid, destination, preset, the cleaned utm_* values, issues (a list of {field, level, code, message}, where level error blocks the URL and warning only suggests a fix such as lowercasing, and code is lowercase, spaces, personal_data, destination_missing or destination_invalid) and presets (the available preset values). Values are cleaned to lowercase without spaces. Use campaigns_hygiene to find messy UTM values that already exist in your traffic and campaigns_list to report on campaigns that have run. To keep a tagged link with a short URL and click counts, use links_create instead.

get.summary: UTM hygiene: near-duplicate values, style issues and unknown sources
get.description: Finds messy UTM values in the traffic of a period so you can fix tagging. Returns period, duplicates, style_issues and unknown_sources. duplicates groups values of utm_source, utm_medium or utm_campaign that differ only by case, spaces or punctuation (Facebook, facebook and face-book), each as {field, suggestion, variants: [{value, visits}]} with the most visited spelling suggested. style_issues lists values that break the lowercase, no-spaces convention as {field, value, visits, suggestion} (up to 50). unknown_sources lists utm_source values that are not a recognized channel as {value, visits} (up to 50). Only the top 500 values per field are scanned. Counts are visits. Suggestions are advice only and nothing is changed. To merge variants into one channel, use channel_rules_create. Takes the shared period and filters inputs. Use campaigns_list for performance and campaigns_builder to create clean tagged URLs.

schema.description: Date range preset, in the site's timezone: today, yesterday, 24h (last 24 hours), 7d, 14d, 28d, 30d, 90d (the last N days), mtd (month to date), last_month, qtd (quarter to date), last_quarter, ytd (year to date), 12mo, last_year, all (all time), or custom (then the range is from to to)
First day of the range as YYYY-MM-DD, in the site's timezone. Only used when period is custom. Without it the range starts 29 days before to
Last day of the range as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only used when period is custom. Without it the range ends today

Also compute a comparison range: previous_period (the same length right before), previous_year (the same dates a year earlier), custom (needs both compare_from and compare_to) or none. Adds the comparison values and the percent change to the result
First day of the comparison range as YYYY-MM-DD. Only used when compare is custom
Last day of the comparison range as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only used when compare is custom
Shift the comparison range so days of the week line up (Monday against Monday)

Filters that must all match: a list of [dimension, operator, value] conditions, e.g. [["country","is","US"],["page","starts_with","/blog"]]. Dimensions: channel, referrer, referrer_url, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term, ref, hostname, country, language, device, browser, browser_version, os, os_version, screen, entry_page, exit_page, interaction, bot_score, page, event, goal, prop:<key>. Use the exact singular names (country, not countries). Values are as stored: country is a two-letter code such as US, channel is a name such as organic_search, a page is a path such as /pricing. Operators taking one value: is, is_not, contains, not_contains, starts_with, wildcard and not_wildcard (the value uses * as a wildcard, e.g. /blog/*), regex and not_regex (a Postgres regular expression of up to 200 characters), gt and lt (a number). any_of and none_of take a list: ["country","any_of",["US","DE"]]. between takes two numbers: ["prop:price","between",[10,50]]. For OR, wrap conditions in an object: {"any":[["channel","is","email"],["utm_medium","is","email"]]}. Up to 20 conditions.
Apply a saved segment by its id (seg_…, from segments_list). Its filters are added to filters
Add imported historical data (dates before the first native event, ignored when filters or a segment are applied)

get.summary: Campaign rollup with conversions, revenue, cost, CPA and ROAS
get.description: Campaign performance report built from utm_campaign, with cost and return on ad spend. Returns period, currency (the site currency), goal_id and goal_name (the goal whose conversions are counted), campaigns, totals and unconverted_costs. Each campaign has visitors, visits, conversions, conversion_rate (percent from 0 to 100, conversions divided by visits), revenue and sources (rows per source and medium with the same metrics). When costs exist (from campaign_costs_list) a campaign also has cost, cpa (cost per conversion, null when there are no conversions) and roas (revenue divided by cost, a ratio such as 2.5, null when there is no cost). Money (revenue, cost, cpa) is an integer in minor units (cents) of the site currency. Costs are matched to campaign names case-insensitively and prorated by days of each month inside the period. A campaign with cost but no traffic is still listed. unconverted_costs lists spend with no exchange rate yet as {campaign, amount_minor, currency} in its own currency, left out of cost, cpa and roas. At most 100 campaigns, busiest first. Only visits with a utm_campaign are included. goal_id defaults to the first active goal, so pass it explicitly to measure a specific goal (ids come from goals_list). Use campaigns_hygiene to clean up names and stats_breakdown with dimension utm_campaign for a plain traffic split.

post.summary: Save a UTM-tagged link to the library
post.description: Saves a UTM-tagged link to the site's link library (path takes site_id). name (up to 120 characters) and destination (an http or https URL up to 2048 characters) are required. The utm values are cleaned automatically, lowercased, trimmed and with spaces turned into underscores, and a value that looks like personal data (an email address for example) is rejected. Up to 20 tags are kept, comma separated entries are split and tags are lowercased and cut at 40 characters. It only stores the link, it does not track anything by itself. The returned url is the destination with the UTM parameters added, and a UTM parameter already in the destination is replaced. Use links_qr for a QR code.

destination.description: Landing page URL, http or https, up to 2048 characters. Existing utm_ parameters in it are replaced by the ones you set

utm_source.description: Where the traffic comes from, e.g. newsletter. Lowercased, trimmed, spaces become underscores. Personal data is rejected

utm_medium.description: Marketing medium, e.g. email or cpc. Lowercased, trimmed, spaces become underscores

utm_campaign.description: Campaign name, e.g. spring_sale. Lowercased, trimmed, spaces become underscores

utm_content.description: Variant, e.g. header_button. Lowercased, trimmed, spaces become underscores

utm_term.description: Paid search keyword. Lowercased, trimmed, spaces become underscores

tags.description: Tags for finding the link later. Up to 20, lowercased and cut at 40 characters. Comma separated entries are split

get.description: Lists the saved campaign links (UTM-tagged URLs) of one site (path takes site_id), newest first and paginated. Each link has id (lnk_...), name, destination, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term, url (the destination with the UTM parameters added, ready to share), tags, notes, created_at and updated_at. query searches name, destination and utm_campaign, tag keeps only links with that tag. The response meta has the pagination plus tags, every tag of the links of the site, sorted. This is the saved library, to see how campaigns performed use campaigns_list or stats_breakdown with dimension utm_campaign.

post.summary: Add a channel rule
post.description: Adds a custom channel rule at the end of the list, so it runs after all existing rules and the built-in taxonomy only applies when no rule matches. channel is the name to assign (up to 32 characters, e.g. Partners). conditions is a non-empty list of objects with field (referrer_host, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, ref or path), operator (is, contains, starts_with or regex) and value. All conditions must match for the rule to apply, and matching is case-insensitive. A condition with a blank value is dropped, and a rule left with no conditions is rejected. A regex that does not compile is rejected. The rule applies to new visits within minutes and does not change history. Use channel_rules_move to reorder and channel_rules_preview to test it. Needs sites.manage.

channel.description: Channel assigned when all conditions match

position.description: Evaluation order (first match wins)

conditions.description: Conditions: field, operator, value

channel.description: Channel name to assign, up to 32 characters, e.g. Partners. Shown as the channel in reports

conditions.description: Non-empty list of conditions that must ALL match for the rule to apply. Each is an object with field, operator and value, e.g. [{"field": "utm_source", "operator": "is", "value": "newsletter"}]. Fields: referrer_host (hostname without www, e.g. news.ycombinator.com), utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, ref (the ref, via or source parameter), path (landing page path, e.g. /pricing). Operators: is (exact), contains, starts_with and regex. Matching is case-insensitive. A condition with an empty value is dropped

get.summary: List channel rules in order
get.description: Lists the custom channel rules of a site in evaluation order (position 1 first). Rules run top to bottom against each new visit and the first rule whose conditions all match decides the channel. A visit that matches no rule gets the built-in channel (direct, organic_search, paid_search, email and so on). Each rule has id (a UUID), channel (the name it assigns), position (1-based), conditions (a list of field, operator and value objects, all of which must match) and created_at. Rules only affect visits recorded after the rule exists and never rewrite old data. Use channel_rules_preview to test a sample visit. Needs analytics.read.

channel.description: Channel assigned when all conditions match

position.description: Evaluation order (first match wins)

conditions.description: Conditions: field, operator, value

delete.summary: Delete a channel rule
delete.description: Deletes a custom channel rule, found by its id from channel_rules_list. Visits it already classified keep their channel, and new visits fall through to the next matching rule or the built-in taxonomy. Remaining rules keep their order. Returns the deleted rule. Needs sites.manage.

Send channel to rename the channel it assigns and conditions to replace the whole conditions list (the list is replaced, not merged, so send every condition you want to keep). Omitted inputs are left alone. Condition fields, operators and regex validity are checked the same way as in channel_rules_create. The change applies to new visits only. To change the order use channel_rules_move. Needs sites.manage.

A rule already at the edge stays put without error. Positions are renumbered 1 to n and the updated rule is returned with its new position. Use channel_rules_list first to see the current order. Needs sites.manage.

post.summary: Preview the channel for a sample referrer and UTM tags
post.description: Dry run that tells you which channel a sample visit would get with the site's current rules. Nothing is stored. Send any of referrer (a URL or bare hostname, www and m prefixes are ignored), utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, ref, path (landing path such as /pricing) and paid_click (true if the URL carried a click id like gclid). The result has channel (the winning channel name), custom_rule (true when a custom rule decided it, false when the built-in taxonomy did) and referrer_host (the cleaned hostname used for matching). A referrer on the site's own domains counts as internal. Use this after channel_rules_create or channel_rules_move to confirm the effect. Needs analytics.read.

get.summary: AI crawlers report: hits by crawler over time, top paths per crawler, by category

This is crawler traffic, not visitor traffic, so it does not appear in stats_breakdown. category is ai (default), search, seo, other or all, and crawler narrows to one named bot such as GPTBot or ClaudeBot. Choose the range with period (default 30d) or custom from and to. The result has period (from and to as dates), category, crawler, totals (hits, distinct paths, distinct crawlers), categories (hits per category, ignoring the category filter), crawlers (up to 50 rows with crawler, category, hits, paths), series (labels per day and daily hits for the top 8 crawlers), top_paths (the 10 most fetched paths for each of the top 8 crawlers), has_data (false until any hits exist) and cloudflare (the connection with zone, status and last_synced_at, or null). Results are cached for up to 30 minutes except right after a Cloudflare change. Needs analytics.read.

get.summary: Data for one card of a custom dashboard
get.description: Returns the live data of one card of a custom dashboard. Dashboards are lists of cards (see dashboards_get for the card list) and each card loads separately, so call this once per card with its position in index, counted from 0. Returns index, type, title, site_id, site_name, params, status and data. status is ok, not_available (the card has nothing to show, for example a funnel card on a site with no funnels or an uptime card with no checks) or no_access (the card belongs to a site your token or role cannot open, and then title, params and data are empty). The shape of data depends on type. metric gives {metric, value, previous, change, period} compared with the previous period. chart gives {metric, interval, period, series: [{date, value}]}. breakdown gives {dimension, label, rows}. goal gives {rows} of goal completions. live gives {visitors}. funnel gives {funnel_id, name, overall_conversion_rate, steps}. uptime gives {checks: [{name, status, uptime}]}. vitals gives {scorecard}. subscriptions gives {currency, mrr_minor, previous_mrr_minor (30 days ago), change (percent, null without MRR 30 days ago), active_subscriptions, subscription_churn_rate (last 30 days)} and is not_available while the site has no payment provider connected. Card params default to period 30d, metric visitors, dimension page and 5 rows (limit is capped at 10). An index outside the list returns 404. Use dashboards_get first to see how many cards there are.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of the item to act on, the id field returned by the tools that list or create it

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Position of the card on the dashboard, counting from 0

post.summary: Create a custom dashboard
post.description: Creates a custom dashboard in a workspace. A custom dashboard is a named, ordered list of up to 40 cards, and the cards can come from different sites of the workspace. Pass name (up to 100 characters) and cards, a list of objects with type (metric, chart, breakdown, goal, live, funnel, uptime, vitals or subscriptions), site_id (pa_..., from sites_list) and optionally title (up to 80 characters) and params. Params used per type are metric (period, metric), chart (period, metric, interval), breakdown (period, dimension, limit), goal (period, limit), funnel (period, funnel_id), uptime (limit) and vitals (period). live and subscriptions take none. Other params are dropped. The period must be a preset such as 30d (not custom) and metric one of visitors, visits, pageviews, views_per_visit, bounce_rate or visit_duration. Every card must point to a site your token can access, and a token limited to some sites must include at least one card. Returns the dashboard with id (dash_...), name, cards and timestamps. Read it with dashboards_get and load each card's numbers with dashboards_card. Needs the content.write permission. The plan sets how many dashboards a workspace has: 1 on Free, 3 on Pro, unlimited on Business. One over the count is refused with a validation error.

cards.description: Cards in order: [{type, site_id, title, params}]. A card for a site you can't access is {type, status: "no_access"}

Cards in order (max 40): [{"type": "metric|chart|breakdown|goal|live|funnel|uptime|vitals|subscriptions", "site_id": "pa_…", "title": "optional", "params": {"period": "30d", "metric": "visitors", "dimension": "page", "funnel_id": "fun_…"}}]. Params a type does not use are ignored

Paginated with page and per_page (max 100). Use dashboards_card to load the data of a card and dashboards_create to add a dashboard. For a single site, stats_overview gives the same kind of numbers without a dashboard.

You need access to every site that has a card on the dashboard, and the dashboard needs at least one card of a site you can access. Returns the deleted dashboard. Use dashboards_update to change a dashboard instead. Ids (dash_...) come from dashboards_list. Needs the content.write permission.

Load the numbers of a card with dashboards_card, using the card's position counted from 0. Ids come from dashboards_list. Send it back unchanged to keep it, it cannot be edited and the last card of such a site cannot be removed. A token limited to some sites cannot leave the dashboard empty. get.summary: List every API operation and MCP tool
get.description: Returns the full catalog of every API operation. Most are MCP tools too, and mcp is false for the ones that are HTTP only or that a person does in the app (deleting data, billing, access and security). Use it to discover which tool or endpoint exists and exactly what it takes. Each item has tool_name, summary, description (nullable), group, verb (HTTP method), path (template with placeholders), permission (the permission a member or token needs, nullable for public tools), mcp (true when it runs as an MCP tool), input_schema (JSON Schema of the inputs) and response_schema (JSON Schema of the response). The response is large. For one tool you already know, prefer the docs pages (docs_search). docs_openapi returns the same information as an OpenAPI document. Public, no authentication needed.

get.summary: List event property keys seen in the last 30 days
get.description: Lists the property keys that custom events carried in the last 30 days, with display settings. Returns a list of {key, events, display_name, hidden, export_safe}. events is how many custom events carried the key (0 for a key that has settings but was not seen recently), display_name is the rename (null when none), hidden says the key is hidden from reports, and export_safe says it is marked as containing no personal data. At most 200 keys are returned, most used first. Pass event to see only keys seen on one raw event name. Property values are never returned here, use stats_breakdown with dimension prop:<key> or events_get for values. Change settings with event_properties_update.

patch.summary: Rename or hide an event property key
patch.description: Renames, hides or marks as export-safe one event property key, for the whole site. Only the inputs you send change. key must be the key as stored (lowercase letters, digits and underscores, up to 64 characters, for example plan). display_name is a label of up to 64 characters (send it empty to remove the rename). hidden removes the key from reports and the event detail pivot while the data is kept. export_safe declares that the key never holds personal data, which includes its values in raw exports and warehouse syncs, so set it only when that is true. Renames and hiding apply when reports are read and rewrite no stored data. Returns {key, display_name, hidden, export_safe}. Needs the sites.manage permission. List the keys with event_properties_list.

key.description: Property key exactly as stored. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores only, 1 to 64 characters, for example plan

display_name.description: Label to show instead of the key, up to 64 characters. Send an empty string to remove the rename

export_safe.description: The key contains no personal data, so it is included in raw exports and warehouse syncs

delete.summary: Delete an event and its history (runs in the background, confirm by typing the name)
delete.description: Permanently deletes a custom event and its whole history. This cannot be undone. The raw event name must be sent twice, in name and again in confirm, as a safety check. Returns {name, status: queued} with HTTP 202 because the rows are removed in the background in batches, so numbers keep changing until it finishes. The event is also hidden right away, and the deletion is recorded in the audit log. Pageviews are not affected. If you only want to stop showing an event, use events_update with hidden true, which keeps the data. Needs the sites.manage permission. Names come from events_list (use the raw_names field if the event was renamed or merged).

name.description: Raw event name to delete, exactly as stored (see raw_names in events_list). All history of this event is deleted

confirm.description: Must be exactly the same text as name, as a safety check. A different value is rejected

get.summary: List events with completions, visits, conversion rate and first/last seen
get.description: The events explorer: every custom event in the period. Returns period, events and hidden. Each event has name (the display name after renames and merges), raw_names (the names the tracker sent), completions, visits, conversion_rate (percent of visits, 0 to 100), revenue (minor units, cents), first_seen and last_seen (ISO 8601 timestamps within the period) and currency (the revenue currency, null when unset). hidden lists events you hid as {name, display_name}. Use search to keep events whose name contains some text. Pageviews are not events here. Use events_get for one event in depth and stats_breakdown with dimension event for a ranked, paginated list. Takes the shared period, compare, filters and segment inputs.

schema.description: Date range preset, in the site's timezone: today, yesterday, 24h (last 24 hours), 7d, 14d, 28d, 30d, 90d (the last N days), mtd (month to date), last_month, qtd (quarter to date), last_quarter, ytd (year to date), 12mo, last_year, all (all time), or custom (then the range is from to to)
First day of the range as YYYY-MM-DD, in the site's timezone. Only used when period is custom. Without it the range starts 29 days before to
Last day of the range as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only used when period is custom. Without it the range ends today

Also compute a comparison range: previous_period (the same length right before), previous_year (the same dates a year earlier), custom (needs both compare_from and compare_to) or none. Adds the comparison values and the percent change to the result
First day of the comparison range as YYYY-MM-DD. Only used when compare is custom
Last day of the comparison range as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only used when compare is custom
Shift the comparison range so days of the week line up (Monday against Monday)

Filters that must all match: a list of [dimension, operator, value] conditions, e.g. [["country","is","US"],["page","starts_with","/blog"]]. Dimensions: channel, referrer, referrer_url, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term, ref, hostname, country, language, device, browser, browser_version, os, os_version, screen, entry_page, exit_page, interaction, bot_score, page, event, goal, prop:<key>. Use the exact singular names (country, not countries). Values are as stored: country is a two-letter code such as US, channel is a name such as organic_search, a page is a path such as /pricing. Operators taking one value: is, is_not, contains, not_contains, starts_with, wildcard and not_wildcard (the value uses * as a wildcard, e.g. /blog/*), regex and not_regex (a Postgres regular expression of up to 200 characters), gt and lt (a number). any_of and none_of take a list: ["country","any_of",["US","DE"]]. between takes two numbers: ["prop:price","between",[10,50]]. For OR, wrap conditions in an object: {"any":[["channel","is","email"],["utm_medium","is","email"]]}. Up to 20 conditions.
Apply a saved segment by its id (seg_…, from segments_list). Its filters are added to filters
Add imported historical data (dates before the first native event, ignored when filters or a segment are applied)
Only events whose name contains this text, case-insensitive

post.summary: Merge several events into one display name
post.description: Merges several raw event names into one display name, for example signup_click and signup_button into Signup. Reports then show a single event with the combined counts. It works when reports are read and the stored events are not changed or deleted. Pass names (the raw names, at least one) and into (the display name). Returns one settings object per merged name, each {name, display_name, hidden, currency, updated_at}. To undo, call events_update for a name with an empty display_name. Needs the sites.manage permission. Names come from events_list (raw_names).

get.summary: One event: chart, property pivot, number property aggregates, pages and sources
get.description: Detail of one custom event. Pass name exactly as shown in events_list (the display name after renames and merges). Returns period, name, raw_names (the stored names behind it), interval, totals, setting, series, property_keys, pivot, numeric, pages, channels and referrers. totals has completions, visits (visits that fired it), revenue (minor units, cents) and conversion_rate (percent of all visits in the period). series is completions per time bucket. setting has display_name, hidden and currency. property_keys lists the property keys seen. patch.summary: Rename, hide or unhide an event, or set its currency
patch.description: Changes how one custom event is shown: rename it with display_name, hide or unhide it with hidden, or set the revenue currency. name is the raw event name as the tracker sent it (see raw_names in events_list). Only the inputs you send change. An empty display_name removes the rename. hidden removes the event from lists and reports while its data is kept. currency is a three-letter ISO 4217 code such as USD, stored in uppercase. This works when reports are read and no stored events are rewritten. Returns {name, display_name, hidden, currency, updated_at}. To combine several events use events_merge, and to erase data use events_delete. Needs the sites.manage permission.

post.summary: Create an experiment as a draft
post.description: Creates an A/B or split URL test for a site. It is saved as a draft and sends no visitor anywhere until a person starts it in the app. Required are name, path (the original page, such as /pricing), goal_id (from goals_list) and variants: a list of { name, path, weight } where the first row is the original page (its path is ignored) and each other row is a page of the same site. Leave every weight out for an even split, or send weights that add up to 100. The Free plan allows one experiment at a time with the original and one variant. Pro and up add more variants, automatic allocation, targeting, a * in the path, secondary goals, a scheduled start and exclusive groups. Requires content.write. Returns the experiment.

paths.description: For kind ad: only on these pages of the site, such as ["/tools/*"]. Empty list means all. Pro and up

get.description: Returns one experiment by id (exp_..., from experiments_list) with its results: per variant the visits, conversions and conversion rate on the goal, and against the original the uplift, the likely range of the difference, the p-value, whether it is significant at the chosen confidence and the chance that it beats the original. results.progress says how far it is from being able to call a winner, and results.mismatch.found true means the visits are not shared out as the weights say, so the result should not be trusted. split breaks the results down by device, channel or country (Pro and up) and humans_only keeps visits the bot score calls likely human (Pro and up). A visit is counted for a variant when it saw that variant, and a conversion counts only after that. Requires analytics.read.

post.summary: Queue an export (built in the background)
post.description: Queues a data export that is built in the background and returns it right away with status queued. Choose it when you need a file (CSV, JSON, XLSX, NDJSON or a ZIP of dashboard panels), and use exports_preview first to check columns and size without creating anything. For lightweight numbers use the stats tools instead. Required inputs are workspace_id (path), site_id, from and to (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, in the export timezone). The kind decides what is exported and which options apply. aggregated (default) gives visit metrics per time bucket and uses grouping, dimensions (up to 6), metrics, filters and segment_id. pageviews, events and raw give one row per hit and use fields, filters and segment_id, require the Pro plan or above, and are limited to 400 days (raw to 93 days). imported gives imported daily stats and uses only dimensions. dashboard gives a ZIP of the overview panels (format zip only). Allowed file_format per kind is csv, json or xlsx for aggregated, pageviews, events and imported, csv or ndjson for raw, and zip for dashboard. Options that do not apply to the chosen kind are ignored. A workspace can have at most 5 exports queued or running at once. The response is the export with id (exp_...), status, row_count and expires_at (null until built). Poll exports_get until status is complete, then call exports_download. The requesting user gets an email when it is ready, a webhook export.ready is sent, and the action is written to the audit log. Event properties in the props column only include properties marked as safe to export (see event_properties_list).

post.summary: Create a funnel
post.description: Creates a funnel, a sequence of steps that visits move through, measured per visit. Pass name and steps, an ordered list of {type, value, match, name}. type is page, event or goal. value is a path for page steps (for example /pricing), a custom event name for event steps, or a goal id (goal_..., from goals_list) for goal steps. match is only for page steps and is exact, prefix, glob (* wildcard) or regex, defaulting to glob when the value has a * and exact otherwise. name is an optional label. Steps with an empty value are dropped. order_mode is strict (each step must come after the previous one, the default) or any (steps in any order). window is visit (the default) or day, and both measure within a single visit because no visitor id is stored. Plan limits apply. Free allows 3 funnels per site and 5 steps, Pro allows 10 steps and Business 20, and a funnel needs at least 2 steps. Returns the funnel with id (fun_...). Read results with funnels_get. Needs the content.write permission.

completed.description: Visits that reached the last step

conversion_rate.description: Completed ÷ entered, %

anyOf.description: Period stats (list only)

name.description: Funnel name, for example Signup flow

steps.description: Ordered steps, at least 2 and up to your plan limit (Free 5, Pro 10, Business 20): [{"type": "page|event|goal", "value": "/pricing | Signup | goal_...", "match": "exact|prefix|glob|regex", "name": "optional label"}]. For page steps value is a path and match defaults to glob when it contains a * and exact otherwise. For event steps value is a custom event name. For goal steps value is a goal id from goals_list. Steps with an empty value are dropped

order_mode.description: strict (default) needs the steps in order, any accepts them in any order

window.description: visit (default) or day. Both measure inside one visit, because no visitor id is stored and a visit never spans a UTC day

get.summary: List funnels with entries, completions and rate
get.description: Lists the funnels of a site with their headline results for the period, ordered by name. Each funnel has id (fun_...), name, steps, order_mode, window and stats {entered, completed, conversion_rate}, where entered is visits that reached step 1, completed is visits that reached the last step and conversion_rate is a percent (0 to 100). Paginated with page and per_page (max 100, default 25). Takes the shared period and filters inputs. For step-by-step detail use funnels_get, and use funnels_create to add one.

schema.description: Date range preset, in the site's timezone: today, yesterday, 24h (last 24 hours), 7d, 14d, 28d, 30d, 90d (the last N days), mtd (month to date), last_month, qtd (quarter to date), last_quarter, ytd (year to date), 12mo, last_year, all (all time), or custom (then the range is from to to)
First day of the range as YYYY-MM-DD, in the site's timezone. Only used when period is custom. Without it the range starts 29 days before to
Last day of the range as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only used when period is custom. Without it the range ends today

Also compute a comparison range: previous_period (the same length right before), previous_year (the same dates a year earlier), custom (needs both compare_from and compare_to) or none. Adds the comparison values and the percent change to the result
First day of the comparison range as YYYY-MM-DD. Only used when compare is custom
Last day of the comparison range as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Only used when compare is custom
Shift the comparison range so days of the week line up (Monday against Monday)

Filters that must all match: a list of [dimension, operator, value] conditions, e.g. [["country","is","US"],["page","starts_with","/blog"]]. Dimensions: channel, referrer, referrer_url, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term, ref, hostname, country, language, device, browser, browser_version, os, os_version, screen, entry_page, exit_page, interaction, bot_score, page, event, goal, prop:<key>. Use the exact singular names (country, not countries). Values are as stored: country is a two-letter code such as US, channel is a name such as organic_search, a page is a path such as /pricing. Operators taking one value: is, is_not, contains, not_contains, starts_with, wildcard and not_wildcard (the value uses * as a wildcard, e.g. /blog/*), regex and not_regex (a Postgres regular expression of up to 200 characters), gt and lt (a number). any_of and none_of take a list: ["country","any_of",["US","DE"]]. between takes two numbers: ["prop:price","between",[10,50]]. For OR, wrap conditions in an object: {"any":[["channel","is","email"],["utm_medium","is","email"]]}. Up to 20 conditions.
Apply a saved segment by its id (seg_…, from segments_list). Its filters are added to filters
Add imported historical data (dates before the first native event, ignored when filters or a segment are applied)
Page number, starting at 1
Funnels per page, 1 to 100. Default 25

post.summary: Invite people by email
post.description: Invites one or more people to a workspace by email and sends each an invitation email with a link that is valid for 14 days. emails is a list of up to 50 addresses (a comma, space or semicolon separated string also works in the app form) and addresses that are already members are skipped, but it is an error when all of them are members. Inviting an address that already has a pending invitation replaces that invitation and sends a new email. role is one of the roles in members_list (default viewer, owner cannot be invited). Use role custom together with custom_role_id (the id from roles_list, Business plan). By default access covers all sites including future ones. To limit access set all_sites to false and list site_ids as public site ids (pa_...). Pending invitations count toward the plan's member limit (Free allows 1 member, the owner) and the call fails when the limit would be exceeded. Invitation emails are rate limited. You cannot grant a role with more permissions or sites than your own. Requires members.manage. Returns the created invitations (see invitations_list for fields).

Everything that uses the segment, such as stats calls with its segment_id, changes straight away. Returns the segment. Ids come from segments_list. Needs the content.write permission.

filters.description: Replacement filters, in the same format as when creating. Filters, all of which must match. Each item is a condition ["dimension", "operator", "value"], or {"any": [conditions]} when any one of several may match. Dimensions: page, entry_page, exit_page, hostname, channel, referrer, referrer_url, ref, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term, country (ISO code, e.g. US), language, device (desktop, mobile, tablet, tv, other), browser, browser_version, os, os_version, screen, interaction (seen, none or unknown), bot_score (likely_human, unsure, likely_bot or not_scored), goal (goal id), event (custom event name) and prop:<key> (custom event property). Operators: is, is_not, contains, not_contains, starts_with, wildcard and not_wildcard (* matches anything), regex, not_regex, any_of and none_of (value is a list), gt and lt (a number), between (a list of two numbers). Rows from the segment form are accepted too: {"dimension", "operator", "value", "property" (for dimension prop), "join": "and" or "or" (or combines the row with the one before it)}. Example: [["country", "is", "US"], ["device", "is", "mobile"], {"any": [["page", "starts_with", "/pricing"], ["goal", "is", "goal_7Q2K9XH3AB"]]}]

Invalid filters return a 422 that names the row. Use it to try filters before segments_create, and stats_aggregate with filters for numbers over another period.

post.summary: Delete all events and visits in a date range (runs in the background, cannot be undone)
post.description: Irreversibly deletes a site's pageviews, custom events and visits for a date range, and cannot be undone. Use it to clear test traffic or remove a bad period. It does not delete the site, its goals or its settings (use sites_delete for the site). from and to are YYYY-MM-DD dates, both inclusive and read in the site's timezone, and to must not be before from. confirm must be the site's domain exactly as shown by sites_get (case does not matter). The request is accepted and returns immediately with status queued, site_id, from and to. The deletion runs in the background in batches, so numbers in the stats tools may take a little while to settle, and there is no status endpoint to poll, check the stats tools until the range is empty. The action is recorded in the audit log. Requires the sites.manage permission.

from.description: First day to delete, YYYY-MM-DD in the site's timezone, inclusive.

to.description: Last day to delete, YYYY-MM-DD in the site's timezone, inclusive. Must not be before from.

confirm.description: The site's domain exactly as shown by sites_get, for example example.com. Case does not matter. Any other value is refused.

get.summary: Filtered traffic summary: bots, traffic rules or PII redactions by reason and country (counts only)
get.description: Counts of hits that were dropped or cleaned before storage, over the last days. Use it to see how much bot traffic, rule-blocked traffic or redaction a site has. Choose kind with bot (hits dropped as bots), rule (hits dropped by traffic rules) or redaction (values redacted by the personal data scrubber). Returns kind, days, total, by_reason, by_country and by_day. by_reason and by_country are lists of {value, count} (up to 50, largest first, value null when unknown) and by_day is a list of {date, count}. days is clamped between 1 and 395 and defaults to 30. These are aggregate counts only. No IP addresses, user agents or redacted values are stored, so nothing can be traced to a person. These hits are not counted as events for billing. Use traffic_rules_list to see or change the rules.

schema.description: bot (hits dropped as bots), rule (hits dropped by traffic rules) or redaction (values cleaned by the personal data scrubber). Default bot

post.summary: Accept a site transfer into one of your workspaces
post.description: Accepts a site transfer invitation and moves the site into one of the caller's workspaces. The token path parameter is from the invitation link, and workspace_id is the destination workspace (ws_...) in which the caller has sites.manage. The caller's own email must match the address the invitation was sent to, and the destination cannot be the workspace the site came from. The site keeps its id, settings, goals and data, but per-member access grants are cleared and its shared links move to the new workspace. It fails when the invitation is no longer pending or has expired, when the destination is at its plan's site limit, or when it already has an active site with the same domain. The move cannot be undone except by transferring back. A token calling this must belong to the destination workspace and have sites.manage. Returns the transfer with status accepted.

Nothing moves until the recipient signs in with that email and accepts (site_transfers_accept), so the site stays here until then. Starting a new transfer cancels any earlier pending one for the same site. email must be a valid address and the recipient picks the destination workspace. Transfer emails are rate limited. Use sites_transfer_cancel to withdraw it. Requires sites.manage. Returns the transfer with site_id, site_domain, from_workspace, to_email, status pending and expires_at.

post.summary: Add a site
post.description: Adds a website to a workspace and returns it, including the tracking snippet to install. The workspace's plan limits the number of sites (Free allows 3) and the call fails with a plan-limit error when it is reached. domain is required and is normalized (for example a full URL or www prefix is reduced to the hostname). name defaults to the domain, timezone defaults to the workspace's timezone (an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin) and currency to the workspace currency (a 3-letter ISO 4217 code such as USD). Side effects are a site.created notification to the workspace's notification channels, a first SEO site audit and domain rating check being queued, and an email with the tracking code to the member who created it (with reminders while no data arrives). Members limited to selected sites who opted into future sites get access to it. Requires sites.manage. Follow up with tracking_snippet or sites_setup_get to install, and tracking_verify to check.

patch.summary: Update site settings
patch.description: Updates settings of a site, changing only the fields you send. Name and identity fields are name, domain (changing it re-checks the domain rating), extra_domains (a list of hostnames) and multi_domain_mode (combined counts one visitor across domains, separate keeps them apart). timezone is an IANA name and currency a 3-letter ISO 4217 code. Privacy fields are honor_dnt, honor_gpc, pii_scrubber, redaction_rules (a list of objects with name and pattern, pattern a regular expression), allowed_params (query parameters to keep), path_masks (a list of objects with pattern and replacement) and bot_filtering. Lists replace the whole existing list. retention_months must not exceed the plan's retention (Free 3 months). traffic_rule_modes maps a rule list (hostnames, paths, referrers, countries, ip_ranges, user_agents or events) to block or allow. vitals_sample_rate is a percentage and the plan caps it (10 on Free, 100 on paid plans). conversion_denominator is visits or visitors. public_dashboard makes stats viewable by anyone with the link and public_indexable lets search engines index that page. Changes take effect for new events within moments. Requires sites.manage. Returns the updated site.

allowed_params.description: Query parameter names kept on stored paths, for example [page, q]. Others are dropped. Replaces the current list.

post.summary: Post an incident update (emails subscribers)
post.description: Publishes an incident update on a status page and, by default, emails its confirmed subscribers. Choose it to announce or update an incident, and use status_page_posts_update to move an existing incident along (for example to resolved) instead of creating a new post. Required is title (max 200 characters). status is one of investigating (default), identified, monitoring or resolved. body is plain text (max 10,000 characters), posted_at is an ISO 8601 time that defaults to now, and notify (default true) controls the email. Emails are only sent for a published page and are rate limited per page, over the limit the post is still published but nobody is emailed. The status_page_id comes from status_pages_list. Needs the uptime.manage permission. Returns the post with id (spp_...), title, body, status, posted_at and updated_at.

post.summary: Create a status page
post.description: Creates a public status page for a workspace that shows chosen uptime checks, incident posts and an email signup. Required is name (max 100 characters). slug (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique across all workspaces) defaults from the name and the page is served at /status/<slug>. check_ids lists the uptime checks to show (upc_... ids from uptime_checks_list) and only checks created with public true are accepted. published defaults to true, so the page is visible to everyone immediately. Optional branding is description (max 2,000 characters), logo_url (must be https), brand_color (hex like #06755b) and custom_domain (a hostname you point a CNAME at the app, unique). Use status_page_posts_create to publish incidents afterwards. Needs the uptime.manage permission. Returns the page with id (sp_...), slug, check_ids and subscribers (count of confirmed subscribers). The plan sets how many pages a workspace has: none on Free (402 plan_limit), 1 on Pro and 10 on Business. A custom_domain and email subscribers need the Business or Enterprise plan. Pages over the plan's count are kept and offline.

post.summary: Create a survey
post.description: Creates a cookieless on-site survey for a site. It collects nothing until its status is active, so create it as draft first or pass status active to start at once. Required are name (internal, visitors never see it, max 120 characters) and questions (1 to 5 rows in order). Each question is an object with key (optional, a stable id of lowercase letters, digits and underscores, generated when omitted), kind (text, choice, multi, rating, nps or yes_no), prompt (required, max 200 characters), required (boolean), choices (a list of up to 10 options, only for choice and multi) and scale (3, 5, 7 or 10, only for rating, default 5). NPS always uses 0 to 10. Targeting is trigger_kind (immediate, delay, scroll, exit or manual) with delay_seconds (0 to 600, default 10, only for delay) and scroll_percent (1 to 100, default 50, only for scroll), paths (rows of match_type exact, prefix or glob and pattern, empty means every page), devices (desktop, mobile, tablet, empty means all), position (bottom_right, bottom_left or center), sample_rate (1 to 100 percent of visitors), thank_you (max 200 characters), starts_on and ends_on (YYYY-MM-DD). Surveys cannot ask for an email address and written answers are scrubbed of personal data. The Free plan allows 1 survey per workspace and a limited number of responses a month, paid plans are unlimited. Needs the content.write permission. Returns the survey with id (svy_...). Read answers with surveys_get.

The result lists up to 12 themes, each with label, count, sentiment (positive, neutral or negative) and example (a representative answer, may be null), plus answers (how many answers were summarized) and generated_at. get.summary: Read the testimonial analytics of a site in one call
get.description: Returns everything the Analytics tab under Testimonials shows for a period: cards (form_views, submissions, completion_rate, answer_rate, widget_views, wall_views, each with previous and change when compare is set), chart (one metric over time), a row per form, request, widget and wall, channels (how forms were opened), pages (where widgets and walls were seen), top_testimonials, new_testimonials (by source and by current status) and countries. post.description: The keeper keeps its status and verified state, and its words unless body_from names another copy. It gains the tags, manual collections, placements and custom properties it lacks. The copies go to the trash marked as merged, and restoring one undoes the merge for that copy. A copy that arrived this month stops counting as a new testimonial. The response carries meta.undo_id.

post.summary: Start an upload, or add a file from a web address
post.description: Two ways. To upload, send filename, content_type and byte_size: the response carries upload, with the url to PUT the file to, the headers to send with it and, for a large file, parts that can be sent one by one. Then call testimonial_media_uploads_finish. Or send source_url and the file is downloaded and processed for you: poll testimonial_media_get until its state is ready. Limits: video and audio up to 500 MB and as long as the plan takes (2 minutes on Pro, 10 minutes on Business, none on Free, where the server responds with 402 plan_limit), images up to 10 MB, a logo up to 2 MB.

post.summary: Create or rotate the crawler log key (shown once)
post.description: Creates a new secret crawler log key (it starts with pik_) for a site and replaces any existing key. The key authenticates uploads of server access logs for the AI crawlers report (POST /api/logs). Use it both to create the first key and to rotate. The new key works at once and the old one stops working at once, so deploy the new key right away to avoid 401s on log uploads. The full key is returned only in this response, in the key field, so store it in a secret store. Afterwards only a short prefix is kept and shown (prefix here, ingest_key_prefix on the site). Returns site_id, key and prefix. Requires sites.manage. Use tracking_ingest_key_revoke to remove the key without replacing it.

key.description: The crawler log key. Shown once: store it now. Send it as a Bearer token to POST /api/logs

delete.summary: Revoke the crawler log key
delete.description: Removes a site's crawler log key. From then on every log upload sent with that key is rejected with 401 until you create a new one with tracking_ingest_key_rotate. Browser tracking with the public site id is not affected. The key cannot be restored. Requires sites.manage. Returns the site object (see sites_get), where ingest_key_prefix is now null.

id.description: Site id used in the tracking snippet

anyOf.description: Start of the crawler log key
Domain Rating from 0 to 100, our own estimate of the strength of the domain's link profile. Null until the first check

post.summary: Check the tracker is installed on the site (script tag, site id, CSP and referrer policy)
post.description: Fetches the site's page and checks that the Privatus Analytics tracking script is installed correctly, and marks the site as verified when the script with this site's id is found. By default it requests the homepage (https://domain/) and url can name another page, but only on the site's own domain, extra domains or their subdomains. The result (under data) has url, status (HTTP status), script_found, site_ids (every data-site id found on the page), installed (true when this site's id is among them), csp and csp_ok (whether the page's Content-Security-Policy lets the tracker load and send), referrer_policy and referrer_ok (a no-referrer policy means every visit shows as direct), and checked_at. It fetches over the public internet, reads at most 2 MB, and is rate limited per workspace and per host, so it responds with 429 when called too often. If the page is unreachable it returns a validation error. Use sites_setup_get to see whether events have arrived. Requires sites.manage.

By default every tracker module is loaded and pageviews are automatic. modules narrows it to a subset of engage (time and scroll), auto (outbound links, downloads, forms, 404s), vitals (Web Vitals), clicks (click maps) and ask (on-site surveys). manual true disables the automatic pageview so you send them yourself. spa sets single-page-app navigation tracking to auto, history, hash or off. domains limits tracking to those hostnames, exclude lists path globs to skip, query_params lists extra query parameters to keep and mask lists client-side path masks written as /u/*->/u/:id. post.summary: Add a traffic rule
post.description: Adds a pattern to one of the site's block or allow lists. list is one of hostnames, paths, referrers, countries, ip_ranges, user_agents or events. pattern uses * as a wildcard and matching is case-insensitive, for example /admin/*, a hostname, a referrer host such as spam.example, a two-letter country code (stored uppercase), a browser name with major version as the user agent is reduced (for example Chrome 120), or a custom event name. ip_ranges take an IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR (203.0.113.0/24), which must be valid. A pattern can exist once per list, and a site can have up to 500 rules. Whether the list blocks or allows matches depends on its mode, which defaults to block and is changed with sites_update. Matching hits are dropped at collection and not stored, and the rule applies within minutes to new hits only. Needs sites.manage. Needs the Pro plan or above (402 plan_limit otherwise).

Each rule has id (a UUID for update and delete), list (hostnames, paths, referrers, countries, ip_ranges, user_agents or events), pattern, label (optional note), mode (block or allow, the mode of that whole list) and created_at. In block mode a hit matching any pattern of the list is dropped, in allow mode a hit matching none is dropped, and an empty list filters nothing. Filter with list. The mode of a list is not set here, it is set with sites_update using traffic_rule_modes. Use traffic_rules_test to check a sample hit. Needs analytics.read.

Use workspace_uptime_checks_create for a check that belongs to no site. kind decides the target. http checks the status code of url, keyword checks that the response body of url contains keyword, tcp connects to host and port, and dns checks that host resolves. Fields for other kinds are ignored. url defaults to the site's home page for http checks. expected_status (100 to 599, default 200), http_method (GET or HEAD) and timeout_seconds (1 to 30, default 20) apply to http and keyword checks. interval_seconds is the time between probes, it must be at least the plan minimum (Free 300, Pro 60, Business 30) and defaults to 300 or the minimum if that is higher. public true lets the check appear on a status page. post.summary: Add a warehouse destination
post.description: Adds a warehouse destination that receives each day's raw events (Business plan only). Daily at 02:00 UTC the previous UTC day is uploaded, the first run is at the next 02:00 UTC, and a failed run is retried an hour later. kind must be given and decides the required settings. s3 (also GCS, R2 and MinIO through endpoint) needs bucket, access_key_id and secret_access_key, with optional region, prefix and endpoint (https, public hosts only). bigquery needs service_account_json, dataset and table, with optional project_id. snowflake needs account, user, private_key (PEM RSA), database, schema and table, with optional warehouse and role. azure needs sas_url (an https blob container SAS link with write permission), with optional prefix. Secrets (secret_access_key, service_account_json, private_key, sas_url) are write only and are never returned. site_ids limits the sites (pa_... ids), empty means every site, and a member or token limited to some sites must name them. Event properties are only sent when marked safe to export (see event_properties_list). Needs the workspace.manage permission. Returns the destination with id (whd_...), a masked target and configured (the names of the filled in settings).

region.description: s3: region, e.g. us-east-1 (auto for R2)

prefix.description: s3 and azure: folder path prefix inside the bucket or container, like privatus/events

service_account_json.description: bigquery only: full service account JSON key text with BigQuery Data Editor access, required for bigquery. Write only, blank keeps the stored key on update

Fields are workspace_id (ws_...), enforce_2fa (members must use two-factor authentication), login_methods (the allowed ones from password, magic_link, passkey, google, github, apple and sso), session_ttl_hours (sign-out after this many hours, null for no limit), app_ip_allowlist (IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to use the app and API, empty means anywhere) and support_access_until (ISO 8601 time until which Privatus Analytics support may view the workspace, null when no access is granted). patch.summary: Update workspace security settings (2FA, login methods, session lifetime, IP allowlist, support access)
patch.description: Changes the workspace security policy, only the inputs you send. enforce_2fa true requires every member to use two-factor authentication and needs the Business plan. login_methods replaces the allowed list with values from password, magic_link, passkey, google, github, apple and sso, and removing a method signs out members' remembered logins so they must log in again. session_ttl_hours signs members out after that many hours (0 removes the limit). app_ip_allowlist replaces the list of IPs or CIDR ranges allowed to reach the app and API (Business plan, an empty list means anywhere) and is refused if it would exclude the IP of the caller, so you cannot lock yourself out. support_access true lets Privatus Analytics support view the workspace for 7 days and false withdraws that access. Requires workspace.manage. Returns the policy (see workspace_security_get).

delete.description: Deletes a workspace together with all of its sites. It is a soft delete, everything disappears at once and is permanently purged after 7 days, so treat it as irreversible.
